title: Hymn 1, sound: jai ghar keerat
hookLine: jai ghar keerat aakheeai kartey kaa hoe beechaaro (Gauri Deepaki M1, ang 12)
last: SOHILA — A SONG OF JOY, FOR THE LAST NIGHT.

cards: Every house has a sound. The kettle in the morning. A television murmuring in the next room.
Somebody's music through a closed door, the same three songs on repeat. A stranger standing in your hallway for an hour with eyes shut would learn a lot about who lives there.
The first hymn of Sohila begins in a house too. Not a temple, not a holy city: any house, named by what is heard inside it.

teach.h: JAI GHAR: IN THE HOUSE WHERE.
teach.b: Here it is, slowly: jai ghar keerat aakheeai, kartey kaa hoe beechaaro. It's Guru Nanak's, in Raag Gauri Deepaki, on Ang 12. Word by word.
Jai ghar: in the house where. Keerat: praise. Aakheeai: is spoken.
Kartey kaa: of the Creator. Hoe beechaaro: and there is reflection, real thought about the One.

So: in the house where the Creator's praise is spoken and reflected on. The next line finishes it: in that house, sing Sohila, and remember the One who made you. Notice the pairing: words said, and words thought about.
Then the refrain, the line the hymn keeps returning to. In paraphrase: sing the song of praise of my Fearless One; I would give myself for that song, which brings lasting peace.
Fearless is nirbhau, the same word you met in the Mool Mantar at the very start of the path. One more layer.

teach.h: GHAR: A BUILDING, AND A HEART.
teach.b: Ghar can mean a building, but in Gurbani it also points inward: the heart, the body, a gathering of people.
Some readers hear it both ways. The house where praise is sung might be a gurdwara, a kitchen, or the inside of one tired person at eleven at night. The Guru doesn't say which house.

how: Sikhs recite Kirtan Sohila at night before sleep, beginning with this hymn of Guru Nanak; in gurdwaras it is sung when the Guru Granth Sahib is closed and laid to rest for the night.

o: honest work, earned by your own hands
a lamp lit at the doorway at night
praise, spoken aloud of the Creator

games.q: the first line, word by word — tap the pairs.

s: the first hymn of Sohila begins by describing a temple
it begins with a house, any house where the Creator's praise is spoken and reflected on.
ghar in Gurbani can point to the heart as well as a building
some readers hear jai ghar as a home and as the person inside it.
the refrain calls the One fearless, nirbhau
the same word that appears in the Mool Mantar.

games.q: the hymn says what makes a house the right place to sing Sohila. what is it?
o: a house that has been specially consecrated.
a house where the Creator's praise is spoken and reflected on.
a house with a copy of the scripture in it.
games.why: the line asks only for praise and reflection together. it names no kind of building at all.

practice: Say the line once just for its sound: jai ghar keerat aakheeai, kartey kaa hoe beechaaro. Say it again and listen to the room around it, a fridge, traffic, a dog, and let the line sit among those sounds.
Then rest in the quiet, and if you pray, whisper it once more.

wordCard.voice: Keerat, praise: the first of Sohila's five, by Guru Nanak: in the house where the Creator's praise is spoken and reflected on, in that house, sing.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: keerat, praise; the word at the center of Sohila's first line.

carryVoice: Your line: jai ghar keerat. In the house where praise is sung. That's day four hundred twenty-two.

sources.ref: Gauri Deepaki M1, Ang 12 (Kirtan Sohila, hymn 1)
